ar: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ ، وَصَلَّى اللَّهُ وَسَلَّمَ وَبَارَكَ عَلَى نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ
translit: Alhamdu lillahi rabbil-alamin, wa sallallahu wa sallama wa baraka ala nabiyyina Muhammadin wa ala alihi wa sahbihi ajmain.
Rabbi-shraḥ lī ṣadrī wa yassir lī amrī wa-ḥlul ʿuqdatam min lisānī yafqahū qawlī

ar: اللَّهُمَّ عَلِّمْنَا مَا يَنْفَعُنَا وَانْفَعْنَا بِمَا عَلَّمْتَنَا وَزِدْنَا عِلْمًا
translit: Allahumma allimna ma yanfa'una wanfa'na bima allamtana wa zidna ilma.

text: Last week we spoke about the childhood of the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] and the years that he spent with his uncle [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]].

And we spoke about the expedition of [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] towards [[Sham|شَام]], towards the greater Syria area, and how [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] as a twelve-year-old boy accompanied him on part of that journey.
But he did not complete the journey, and we spoke about that story last week about the encounter that they had with the Christian monk [[Buhayra|بَحِيرَى]].

And how [[Buhayra|بَحِيرَى]] saw the signs of prophethood on the Prophet [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] even though he was a young boy—he was only twelve years old at the time.

And then [[Buhayra|بَحِيرَى]] advised [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] not to allow [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] to accompany the rest of the caravan to [[Sham|شَام]] because he said, there are Jews in that place who will see this boy and they will recognize him just as I recognized him.
And they will know that he is the one who was prophesied in the previous scriptures, in the previous revelations.

But once they realize that he is not from [[Bani Isra'il|بَنِي إِسْرَائِيل]], once they realize that he is not from the progeny of [[Ya'qub|يَعْقُوب]] [[alayhis-salam|عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام]], rather he is from [[Bani Ismail|بَنِي إِسْمَاعِيل]], from the progeny of [[Ismail|إِسْمَاعِيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام]], they will be jealous and they will kill him.
"So don't take him to [[Sham|شَام]], send him back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]." So he was sent back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
So this happened when he was around twelve years old. So he lived in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], he continued to live there with his uncle, and he grew up in a very honorable way.
Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] protected him, even in his childhood, from any type of bad behavior.
Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] did not allow [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] even to witness any type of bad behavior.
And he grew up with the best character and the best morals, and he grew up with complete honesty, and complete truthfulness, and complete sincerity.
So he combined all the good characteristics that a person could have, even in his childhood.
So when he grew up to be a little bit older—he was about twenty years old, young man—a very important event took place in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
A great event took place in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] when the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] was about twenty years old.
And this event is known as [[Harb al-Fijar|حَرْبُ الْفِجَار]], [[Harb al-Fijar|حَرْبُ الْفِجَار]].
And the reason why it was called [[Harb al-Fijar|حَرْبُ الْفِجَار]]—we'll get to the reasoning behind that in a minute [[insha'Allah|إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ]].
The word [[al-Fijar|الْفِجَار]], it comes from [[al-fujur|الْفُجُور]], and [[fujur|فُجُور]] means to do something evil, to do something that is wrong.
So this is where this war got its name from, [[Harb al-Fijar|حَرْبُ الْفِجَار]].
And who is the one who did something wrong, who started this war? We'll get into that in a minute [[insha'Allah|إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ]].
So basically this war, it was between a tribe called [[Hawazin|هَوَازِن]], which was a tribe from outside of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], and between the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]].
And the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], of course, were from inside [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]. So this war was between [[Hawazin|هَوَازِن]] and [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]].

Now we know that there are four months that are considered the sacred months: those are the months of [[Rajab|رَجَب]], [[Dhu al-Qa'dah|ذُو الْقَعْدَة]], [[Dhu al-Hijjah|ذُو الْحِجَّة]], and [[Muharram|مُحَرَّم]].
These are [[al-Ashhur al-Hurum|الأَشْهُرُ الْحُرُم]], the sacred months.
And they were made sacred by Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] when He created the heavens and the earth.

Before the creation of mankind, when Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] created the heavens and the earth, He made these four months sacred: [[Rajab|رَجَب]], [[Dhu al-Qa'dah|ذُو الْقَعْدَة]], [[Dhu al-Hijjah|ذُو الْحِجَّة]], and [[Muharram|مُحَرَّم]].
So what does it mean, these months are sacred? It means it is not permissible to start fighting, to start a war during these four months.
But if someone starts a war with you, then you are allowed, of course, to defend yourself.

So the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they respected this. And remember, the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] originally, the Arabs beforehand, they were on the religion of [[Ibrahim|إِبْرَاهِيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام]].

But as we spoke about earlier, [[Amr ibn Luhayy|عَمْرُو بْنُ لُحَيّ]], he brought idol worship back into the Arabian Peninsula, so the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they were idol worshippers, but they had still some remnants of the religion of [[Ibrahim|إِبْرَاهِيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام]] still with them.

Even though their [[tawhid|تَوْحِيد]] was not there—they used to worship idols—they still had some pieces of the religion of [[Ibrahim|إِبْرَاهِيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام]] with them that they used to observe. For example, [[Hajj|حَجّ]] still used to take place.
And also [[al-Ashhur al-Hurum|الأَشْهُرُ الْحُرُم]], these four sacred months were still considered sacred by the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]].
So they would not even think about starting any fighting or starting any war at this time.
They considered it something that was impermissible, and they considered it something that was out of the question—they would never even think of starting a war at that time.

It was such to the extent that if somebody had murdered another person's father and then they went into hiding, and when the [[al-Ashhur al-Hurum|الأَشْهُرُ الْحُرُم]] came—when these four sacred months came—if this man who murdered another person's father, if he came out of hiding and the son of the murdered person saw the murderer of his father, he would not even touch him.
"Oh no, we can't do it. These are the four holy months, we cannot do anything in this time."
So they respected it to that extent, that they would not even touch the murderer of their own father if they happened to see him during this time.
But the tribe of [[Hawazin|هَوَازِن]], they decided that they would take advantage of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]]'s respect for these sacred months.

They thought to themselves, "Look, the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], during these four months, they're never even going to think about starting a fight, and they would not expect anyone else from the Arabs to fight them as well."
"They think that we all think like them. Because they consider it sacred, they probably assume that all of the other Arabs, they will consider it sacred as well and they will respect that as well."
So the [[Hawazin|هَوَازِن]], they decided to take advantage of this.
So they attacked the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] during [[al-Ashhur al-Hurum|الأَشْهُرُ الْحُرُم]], during the sacred months.
And the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they were not expecting this. It came totally out of the blue. It came to them as a surprise attack, so they were attacked.
And that is why it is called [[Harb al-Fijar|حَرْبُ الْفِجَار]].
As we said, [[al-Fijar|الْفِجَار]], it comes from [[fujur|فُجُور]], meaning to commit an act of evil.

And who is the one who committed the act of evil? [[Hawazin|هَوَازِن]], the tribe of [[Hawazin|هَوَازِن]], for starting an act of aggression, starting a war during the sacred months. This is an act of [[fujur|فُجُور]], this is an act of evil.
And that is why these wars became known as [[Harb al-Fijar|حَرْبُ الْفِجَار]].
And it happened in the history of the Arabs five times. There were five instances of [[Harb al-Fijar|حَرْبُ الْفِجَار]].
And one of them happened during the time that the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] was about twenty years old.
So this is still about twenty years before he receives the first revelation—he's a young man.
So [[Hawazin|هَوَازِن]], they attack [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], and of course [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they are defending themselves.
So the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] witnessed this battle with his own eyes, and he participated with the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] to some extent.
He didn't actually fight, he didn't actually fight, but he would give the arrows to his uncles.

The uncles of the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]], they were fighting, and the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] was right there in the middle of the battlefield, and he would give the arrows to his uncles for his uncles to shoot.
So this was the extent of the participation of the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] in the defense of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] in [[Harb al-Fijar|حَرْبُ الْفِجَار]].

So as we mentioned before, everything that happened in the life of the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]], it happened for some wisdom that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] decreed.
And it was preparing him for something that would happen in the future, like the fact that the Prophet [[ṣallallāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam|ﷺ]] grew up as an orphan—he was an orphan, right?
